market_story: hydro: ~43% of CISO's conventional-hydro plants (10-12% of the energy) are run-of-river/canal/Corps-dam release-takers whose output follows inflow and water deliveries, not price - they physically cannot park at zero in the solar belly and surge overnight, so the fleet's diurnal swing is muted relative to a fully-optimizing pool (measured fleet hourly p5 738-954 MW, never near zero). The reservoir class (Big Creek, SWP, the Pit/Feather cascades) shapes within FERC-licence minimum releases: the reconciled Q95 floor is that sustained base, and removing the RoR budget from the shapeable pool raises the reservoir pool's marginal water value into the overnight price band - which is why the fleet no longer rides the p95 capability ceiling all night. The remaining evening under-dispatch is the model's compressed evening-overnight price premium (~half the real spread) under-rewarding evening water - a price-formation defect of the intertie/scarcity representation, not of the water physics.
